# Synthetic Persona Pretraining: Alignment from Token Zero

**Link:** https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.13482  ·  **Code/Data:** https://github.com/epfl-dlab/spp · https://huggingface.co/dlab-spp · https://modelraising.ai/spp/
**Authors:** Minder, Moskvoretskii, Singhal et al. (EPFL dlab; Toronto; Northeastern; MATS)  ·  **Venue/Date:** arXiv, Aug 2026

## Gist
- Instead of grafting an assistant persona on after pretraining, grow it from the first token: annotate ~10% of pretraining documents with first-person, constitution-grounded "reflections" marked by an `<assistant>` token, then "bind" the post-trained assistant to that persona.
- At 1.7B/100B-token and 33B/500B-token scale, SPP from token zero (SPP{T0}) beats vanilla and filtered pretraining on constitution adherence, moral-dilemma alignment and jailbreak robustness, with capabilities preserved and over-refusal lower than a safety-tuned baseline.
- The token-zero advantage grows with scale on hard/OOD value evals (~2 -> ~18 points on AI Risk vs vanilla from 1.7B to 33B); midtraining-only reflections (SPP{MT}) give jailbreak robustness but not value internalisation.
- Fragile where it matters: refusal-direction ablation and chat-template removal destroy the jailbreak gains, while value alignment survives.

## Setup & technical details
- Annotation: 51.4M docs (~10% of tokens). All "harmful" docs (safety score >=3; 27.6B tokens, 5.5% of budget) plus an equal-token benign sample. Reflections average 53 tokens (cap 128), inserted at random points conditioned only on preceding text, generated by Qwen3.5-35B-A3B from a constitution; +2.7B tokens (0.55%). Loss on both document and reflection tokens, excluding the `<assistant>` token.
- Variants: Vanilla; Filtered (harmful docs loss-masked); SPP{T0}; SPP{MT} (cooldown only); SPP{T0,MT}.
- Persona binding (SP-SFT): 300k single-turn conversations, 90% WildChat prompts, 10% safety (WildJailbreak + WildGuardMix), responses generated under the same constitution.
- Evals: ConstitutionEval (4-choice, easy/hard); AIRiskDilemmas (16 value axes, misalignment rate); 8 jailbreak benchmarks incl. AdvBench, StrongREJECT, FORTRESS, PAP, DAN, JBB, adaptive PAIR and PEZ (ASR worst@5); OR-Bench/XSTest over-refusal; standard capability suite.

## Methods / techniques
- **Reflection annotation**: in-document persona voice that comments on content in the model's own first person, citing constitution articles. Recipe for injecting a persona into pretraining distribution without changing the documents.
- **Persona binding**: SFT whose response distribution matches the pretraining persona; the paper shows binding only works when distributions match (Figure 4).
- **Constitution-citation held-out test**: hold out articles from SP-SFT, check whether the model still cites them (SPP{T0} 21% vs vanilla 0%); an interpretability-style probe of where the values came from.
- **Robustness perturbations**: refusal-direction abliteration (Arditi et al. 2024) and swapping the `<assistant>` token for a standard chat template.
- **Continual-training stress test** on ChemPile with and without 5% safety replay.

## Key results
- ConstitutionEval-Hard: SPP{T0} ~10 points over SPP{MT}; SPP{MT} over vanilla 7 (1.7B) -> 14 (33B).
- AIRiskDilemmas: SPP{T0} over SPP{MT} ~4 -> ~19 points (1.7B -> 33B); over vanilla ~2 -> ~18. Token-zero models rank Truthfulness and Justice highest; baselines rank Learning and Creativity.
- Jailbreaks: all SPP variants lower ASR than baselines; SPP{MT} and SPP{T0,MT} more robust than SPP{T0} alone (recency bias). Robustness plateaus after ~5% safety fraction in SFT; value alignment barely depends on SFT safety fraction (0-60%).
- Over-refusal 13.6-17.2% (1.7B) vs SafeLM 33.2%.
- Ablations at 1.7B: third-person reflections ~ vanilla; refusal rationales help AI Risk, hurt ConstitutionEval; end-of-document placement worse.
- Continual training without replay: JBB-direct ASR rises to 20-60% for all models; 5% replay restores.
- Abliteration: all models lose refusals, SPP loses most; values survive. Template removal: jailbreak gains gone, value gains mostly intact for T0 models.

## Insights & takeaways
- "Values" and "refusals" are separable: pretraining shapes the former deeply; the latter sits in a thin, ablatable direction regardless of when you trained it.
- Persona is a *training-distribution* object: binding fails if post-training responses do not match the pretraining persona's distribution. This is a mechanistic claim about why post-hoc alignment feels shallow.
- Recency matters for behaviour, depth matters for values: midtraining is enough for refusals, token zero for generalising values.

## Relevance to my research
- Training-stage decomposition: this is the cleanest manipulation of *when* a persona enters. Released checkpoints (1.7B/33B, vanilla vs SPP) are a ready model-organism pair for asking whether persona directions (Assistant Axis style) are present in base weights or only after binding.
- Project C: "persona gates expression" meets "persona bound in pretraining". Hypothesis: an SPP{T0} model's gate should be harder to open with a dismissive system prompt than vanilla's. Also a test of whether Story Imprinting (traits absorbed from resembling characters) is weaker when the assistant persona is defined from token zero.
- Refusal-vs-values separation is a say-vs-do analogue: the model can keep "values" (probe-decodable, MCQ) while losing refusal behaviour. Reuse their abliteration + ConstitutionEval pairing as a template for "does the grudge survive ablating the affect direction?".
- Project D / affect-as-attack-surface: the `<assistant>` token as persona switch is a single-token gate; its removal collapses safety. Analogous single-cue gates (author name in Project A) deserve the same perturbation test.

## Caveats & critiques
- Largest model is 33B on 500B tokens; frontier generalisation unknown, and midtraining variants show a small capability drop at 33B absent at 1.7B.
- Reflections are LLM-generated from one constitution; the "constitution adherence" eval is built from the same constitution, so part of the gain is in-distribution.
- No RL stage; whether binding survives RLHF/RLVR is explicitly open.
- Jailbreak robustness is the fragile part, and that is the part most buyers want.
- Interpretability analysis is behavioural perturbation, not circuit-level; no persona-direction analysis despite the natural fit.

## Related
- [[The Assistant Axis - Situating and Stabilizing the Default Persona of Language Models]] - the default persona SPP tries to install early; Assistant Axis found its structure already in base models, which SPP would sharpen.
- [[Refusal Lives Downstream of Persona in Chat Models]] - consistent with SPP's finding that refusals ablate away while persona-level values persist.
- [[When Role-playing, Do Models Believe What They Say]] - asks the same depth question (representation vs behaviour) for post-training interventions.
